relevance_reason: The title says the paper reports a family with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia linked to LEF1-related disorders, which is the subject of ECTD17. Only the title was available, so no details could be extracted.

findings.statement: Hassan et al. (2024) reported a family with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia, which they considered to expand the spectrum of LEF1-related disorders.
quotes: Hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia in a family: expanding spectrum of LEF1-related disorders.

relevance_reason: This paper first describes the ECTD17 syndrome: patients with monoallelic and biallelic LEF1 variants who have ectodermal dysplasia and limb malformations.

findings.statement: Dufour et al. (2022) concluded that monoallelic and biallelic variants in LEF1, which encodes a transcription factor acting downstream of the WNT-beta-catenin signaling pathway, cause a novel syndrome of limb malformations and ectodermal dysplasia.
quotes: Our findings establish mono- and biallelic variants in LEF1 as a cause for a novel syndrome comprising limb malformations and ectodermal dysplasia.
LEF1 encodes a transcription factor acting downstream of the WNT-β-catenin signaling pathway.

findings.statement: Dufour et al. (2022) reported 12 individuals with LEF1 variants: 11 from 4 unrelated families and 1 from a consanguineous family. The phenotypic spectrum included ectodermal dysplasia and various limb malformations, such as radial ray defects, polydactyly, or split hand/foot.
quotes: We report on 12 individuals harboring LEF1 variants.
The phenotypic spectrum includes various limb malformations, such as radial ray defects, polydactyly or split hand/foot, and ectodermal dysplasia.

findings.statement: Dufour et al. (2022) stated that, depending on the type and location of the LEF1 variant, this condition can be inherited in either an autosomal dominant or an autosomal recessive manner.
quotes: Depending on the type and location of LEF1 variants, the inheritance of this novel Mendelian condition can be either autosomal dominant or recessive.

findings.statement: Using high-throughput sequencing, Dufour et al. (2022) found monoallelic LEF1 variants in 11 affected individuals from 4 unrelated families. They also found a biallelic LEF1 variant in an affected individual from a consanguineous family. Earlier, LEF1 had been suspected as a candidate gene for ectodermal dysplasia in 2 individuals with 4q35 microdeletions.
quotes: Monoallelic variants in LEF1 were detected in 11 affected individuals from 4 unrelated families, and a biallelic variant was detected in an affected individual from a consanguineous family.
It was recently suspected as a candidate for ectodermal dysplasia in 2 individuals carrying 4q35 microdeletions.

findings.statement: Functional studies by Dufour et al. (2022) used immunofluorescence, immunoblotting, pulldown assays, and RNA sequencing. The authors suggested 2 molecular mechanisms. Haploinsufficiency or loss of DNA binding was responsible for a mild to moderate phenotype, whereas loss of beta-catenin binding caused by biallelic variants was associated with a severe phenotype.
quotes: Our functional data indicate that 2 molecular mechanisms are at play: haploinsufficiency or loss of DNA binding are responsible for a mild to moderate phenotype, whereas loss of β-catenin binding caused by biallelic variants is associated with a severe phenotype.

findings.statement: Transcriptomic studies by Dufour et al. (2022) showed altered WNT signaling associated with the LEF1 variants.
quotes: Transcriptomic studies reveal an alteration of WNT signaling.

relevance_reason: Reports two patients with de novo 4q25 deletions encompassing LEF1 who had hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia, and proposes LEF1 haploinsufficiency as the cause of ECTD17.

findings.statement: Lévy et al. (2020) reported 2 unrelated patients with severe oligodontia affecting both primary and permanent teeth, hypotrichosis and hypohidrosis, consistent with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia. Both patients also had taurodontism and a particular alveolar bone defect.
quotes: We report two unrelated patients with 4q25 de novo deletion encompassing LEF1, associated with severe oligodontia of primary and permanent dentition, hypotrichosis and hypohidrosis compatible with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia.
Taurodontism and a particular alveolar bone defect were also observed in both patients.

phenotypes.text: severe oligodontia of primary and permanent dentition

findings.statement: In 2 unrelated patients with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia, Lévy et al. (2020) identified de novo deletions at chromosome 4q25 that included the LEF1 gene. The authors concluded that the findings provided further evidence that LEF1 haploinsufficiency causes ectodermal dysplasia. They noted that no pathogenic variants involving LEF1 had previously been reported in humans.
quotes: We report two unrelated patients with 4q25 de novo deletion encompassing LEF1
So far, no pathogenic variants or variations involving the LEF1 gene have been reported in human.
We provide further evidence for LEF1 haploinsufficiency role in ectodermal dysplasia and delineate its clinical phenotype.

findings.statement: Lévy et al. (2020) noted that, in mice, targeted inactivation of the Lef1 gene completely blocks the development of multiple ectodermal appendages.
quotes: In mice, targeted inactivation of the LEF1 gene results in a complete block of development of multiple ectodermal appendages.

relevance_reason: Mouse study of LEF1 function in somitogenesis and Notch/Dll1 regulation; it adds context on LEF1 gene function but reports no ectodermal dysplasia or limb phenotype and no human patients.

findings.statement: Galceran et al. (2004) showed that in mice, a targeted mutation of Lef1 affected the patterning of somites and the expression of components of the Notch pathway. The mutation abrogated LEF1 function and impaired the activity of coexpressed TCF factors.
quotes: a targeted mutation of Lef1, which abrogates LEF1 function and impairs the activity of coexpressed TCF factors, affects the patterning of somites and the expression of components of the Notch pathway

findings.statement: Galceran et al. (2004) found that LEF1 bound multiple sites in the Dll1 promoter both in vitro and in vivo. Mutating these LEF1-binding sites impaired expression of a Dll1-LacZ transgene in the presomitic mesoderm. Induced expression of LEF1-beta-catenin activated endogenous Dll1 expression in fibroblastic cells. The authors concluded that Wnt signaling can affect the Notch pathway through LEF1-mediated regulation of Dll1.
quotes: LEF1 was found to bind multiple sites in the Dll1 promoter in vitro and in vivo.
mutations of LEF1-binding sites in the Dll1 promoter impair expression of a Dll1-LacZ transgene in the presomitic mesoderm
Thus, Wnt signaling can affect the Notch pathway by a LEF1-mediated regulation of Dll1.
